name: Julia Brim-Edwards

bio.statement: Brim-Edwards currently serves as Multnomah County's District 3 Commissioner.
In her voters' pamphlet statement, Brim-Edwards lists her occupational background as a Nike senior director and small business owner.
bio.excerpt: Senior Director, Nike; Small business owner

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

bio.statement: Brim-Edwards's pamphlet statement lists a bachelor's degree from Oregon State University.
bio.excerpt: Oregon State University, BA; Washington-Monroe HS

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

bio.statement: Her pamphlet statement lists prior service as an OSU trustee, on Head Start and school boards, and as U.S. Senate legislative staff.
bio.excerpt: OSU Board Trustee; Head Start Board, School Board; Legislative, U.S. Senate staff

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

positions.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, Brim-Edwards says she would connect more people with mental illness and addiction to treatment, services and housing.
positions.excerpt: Connect more people struggling with mental health and addiction to treatment, services, and housing.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement says Brim-Edwards will work with labor and business for more jobs with benefits.
positions.excerpt: Julia will work with labor and business for more good jobs with benefits.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement calls for reducing layers of local taxes and fees to make life more affordable.
positions.excerpt: Reduce layers of local taxes and fees, making life more affordable.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement calls for requiring county-funded contractors to be transparent and accountable for results and spending.
positions.excerpt: Require County-funded contractors be transparent and accountable for their results and how taxpayer dollars are spent.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

positions.statement: Her pamphlet statement pledges to protect healthcare, food assistance and immigrant neighbors.
positions.excerpt: Protect healthcare, food assistance and our immigrant neighbors.

source.publisher: Multnomah County Elections (Voters' Pamphlet, Nov 3 2026, large print)

positions.statement: Brim-Edwards's campaign site cites her record on reducing unsheltered homelessness, increasing housing access and ending street encampments.
positions.excerpt: reducing unsheltered homelessness, increasing access to housing, ending street encampments, and more effectively managing our funds.

positions.statement: Willamette Week reported in February 2026 that Brim-Edwards says the county must require drug offenders to seek treatment.
positions.excerpt: The county must require offenders to seek treatment, Brim-Edwards says,

positions.statement: In a February 2026 OPB report, Brim-Edwards said the county needs a leader to rebuild trust and get it on the right track.
positions.excerpt: The County needs a proven, effective and collegial leader to rebuild trust and get the County on the right track

gaps: No voting record collected (county board votes not in scope of fixed search set)

verification_summary.balance_notes: All three candidates have T1 pamphlet items plus T2 campaign-site items and T3 coverage (Singleton 5 bio/8 positions, Brim-Edwards 4/8, Meieran 4/9). Coverage comparable. Meieran's T2 items come from fix-multco.com (confirmed via an OPB link); her pamphlet website fixmultco.com and filing website SharonforChair.com could not be fetched. Missed T3: Portland Mercury 2026-03-10 'Inside the race for county chair' (Singleton and Brim-Edwards, pre-dates Meieran's entry) not used.
